config.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes

intro.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a small web application with multiple pages, where some pages are nested inside others and some require user authentication to access. You'll learn how to organize your app's structure using nested routes to create parent-child page relationships. The core concepts involve using React Router's Route components to define these nested paths and creating a protected route component that checks login status before allowing access. You'll work with React components, TypeScript for type safety, and React Router's hooks and components to manage navigation and route protection in a beginner-friendly way.
intro.usecase: Nested and protected routes are essential for building secure, organized applications with complex user interfaces. For example, in a dashboard product like an analytics platform, nested routes allow you to structure the main dashboard layout while rendering different report panels (like 'Overview', 'Users', 'Revenue') within it without reloading the entire page. Protected routes ensure that only authenticated users can access sensitive areas, such as admin settings or billing pages, redirecting unauthenticated visitors to a login screen. This pattern is also common in e-commerce sites, where a product page might nest routes for reviews, specifications, and related items, while protecting the checkout and order history routes.

objectives: Construct a nested route structure using React Router's <Outlet> component
Configure route parameters to pass data between parent and child components
Implement a protected route component that conditionally renders based on authentication state
Integrate authentication context with route protection logic
Manipulate navigation flow by redirecting unauthorized users to a login page
Initialize nested layouts that maintain consistent UI across related routes
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define and validate route parameter types

steps.instruction: Import React, BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link, Navigate, and Outlet from their respective packages to enable routing functionality.
steps.hint: You'll need to import React from 'react' and the routing components from 'react-router-dom'.

steps.title: Create a basic authentication context
steps.instruction: Define an interface for the authentication context value, including a boolean `isAuthenticated` and a function `login` that returns void. Then, create an AuthContext using React.createContext with a default value that matches this interface.
steps.hint: Use `interface` to define the shape of your context value. Provide a default value for the context that matches your interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface for your authentication context and a React context created with a default value.
successCriteria: An interface named AuthContextValue is defined with `isAuthenticated: boolean` and `login: () => void`. An AuthContext is created using React.createContext with a default value matching the interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your interface includes both `isAuthenticated` and `login`, and that your context uses React.createContext with a default value that matches the interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: define an interface for the context value and create the AuthContext with React.createContext.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state in the context
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthContext provider component, create a state variable named 'isAuthenticated' using useState, initialized to false.
steps.hint: Use useState to declare a boolean state variable. The initial value should be false since the user starts logged out.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state initialization
const [isLoggedIn, setIsLoggedIn] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: A state variable 'isAuthenticated' is declared with an initial value of false.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with false as the initial value, and the state variable is named 'isAuthenticated'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using useState with the correct initial value (false) and naming the variable 'isAuthenticated'.
steps.feedbackWrong: declare a state variable inside the component using useState(false).

steps.title: Create a ProtectedRoute component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ProtectedRoute that takes props including a 'children' prop and returns the children directly for now.
steps.hint: Define a component that accepts props and returns props.children. You'll add authentication logic in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ProtectedRoute component is defined and ready to be enhanced with authentication logic.
successCriteria: ProtectedRoute component is created as a functional component that accepts children and returns them.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a component named ProtectedRoute that returns props.children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProtectedRoute component wasn't created correctly. Create a functional component named ProtectedRoute that returns its children.

steps.instruction: Inside your Dashboard component, import the Outlet component from 'react-router-dom' and place it where you want nested route content to appear.
steps.hint: Import Outlet from react-router-dom and add it as a JSX element in your Dashboard's return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component will have an Outlet imported and placed, ready to render nested route content.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Set up the main App component with Router
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that wraps your application with BrowserRouter and defines a basic Routes structure.
steps.hint: Start by creating the App component function. Inside it, return a BrowserRouter component containing a Routes component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is created and returns a BrowserRouter with a Routes component inside it.

steps.title: Define public routes in the App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, add Route components for Home and Login pages that are accessible without authentication.

steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have two public routes: one for the Home page and one for the Login page.
successCriteria: Two Route components are added inside the Routes element with paths '/' and '/login', and corresponding Home and Login components are defined and used.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some public routes, but make sure both Home and Login routes are present with correct paths and elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The public routes are not correctly defined. Ensure you have Route components for both Home and Login pages inside the Routes element.

steps.title: Implement protected nested routes structure
steps.instruction: In the App component's Routes, wrap the Dashboard route with ProtectedRoute and define nested routes for Profile and Settings inside it using the Route component.
steps.hint: Use the ProtectedRoute component as a wrapper element around a Route component. Inside ProtectedRoute, define nested routes using the Route component with path and element props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component's Routes will include a ProtectedRoute wrapping the Dashboard route, with nested Profile and Settings routes defined inside.
successCriteria: ProtectedRoute wraps a Route component with path='/dashboard' and element={<Dashboard />}. Inside ProtectedRoute, there are nested Route components for '/dashboard/profile' and '/dashboard/settings'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure ProtectedRoute wraps the Dashboard route and contains the nested Profile and Settings routes inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nested routes structure isn't quite right. Remember to wrap the Dashboard route with ProtectedRoute and define the nested Profile and Settings routes inside it.

steps.title: Add navigation links with authentication awareness
steps.instruction: In the App component, add a navigation section with Link components that conditionally show/hide based on the authentication state from AuthContext.
steps.hint: You'll need to import Link from react-router-dom and use the AuthContext to access isAuthenticated. Create a nav element with conditional links for Home, Login, and Dashboard.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will include a navigation section with conditional links that respond to authentication status.
successCriteria: Navigation section with Link components is added to App component, showing Login link when not authenticated and Dashboard link when authenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some navigation elements, but make sure to conditionally show/hide links based on isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation section is missing or doesn't properly use conditional rendering with authentication state.

steps.title: Wire up authentication toggle functionality
steps.instruction: In the App component, add a button that calls the login function from the authentication context to toggle authentication state.
steps.hint: You'll need to use the useContext hook to access the AuthContext and its login function, then add a button with an onClick handler that calls it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the App component that, when clicked, triggers the authentication toggle via the context's login function.
successCriteria: The App component includes a button with an onClick handler that calls the login function from AuthContext.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button's onClick handler correctly calls the login function from the AuthContext.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication toggle isn't wired correctly. Check that you're using useContext to access AuthContext and calling its login function in the button's onClick.
